subject: Apportionment / proration request — GCP & Azure listing charge alignment
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marketplace Billing <billing@marketplace.example.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Apportionment/proration for Sept — GCP + Azure listing overlap

Hi team,

Quick one — AtlasHealth flagged a discrepancy between the Marketplace invoice we received for September and the usage stamps in their ledger. They have two active listings (GCP and Azure) that were cross-listed mid-month (cutover 2026-09-17) and it looks like the metering window produced overlapping usage for the 17th–19th.

Can you send: 1) the raw per-day per-sku metering export for AtlasHealth (CSV) for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30, 2) the signed invoice PDF you have for Sept, and 3) any notes on how you applied proration on the cutover date?

We need the evidence bundle to propose a customer credit or internal reallocation if the overlap caused double-billing into our marketplace payout. HubSpot: deal 56432; please include any internal ticket references.

CCing Karthik/Rishi to handle marketplace-side apportionment once we have the files.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Marketplace Billing <billing@marketplace.example.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marketplace Partner Ops <partner-ops@cloudmarket.example.net>
Date: 2026-10-19T07:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Apportionment/proration for Sept — GCP + Azure listing overlap

Hi Irene,

Thanks for flagging. Attaching the per-day metering export and the invoice PDF we have on file. Notes below:

- Attachments: usage_report_202609.csv, invoice_202609_marketplace.pdf
- For cutovers we apply entity-level proration at the SKU-id boundary using UTC timestamps; the process can result in a one-day overlap when listings are marked active across two cloud providers because we reconcile by listing-id and then by raw usage timestamp.
- We do not automatically dedupe across two different listings even when they represent the same product across clouds — that’s something we can do via a partner reconciliation if both listings are linked to the same seller entity.

If you want us to produce a deduped view (apportioned to the listing that was elected as primary on cutover), we can run a job and return a corrected CSV + credit memo draft. This will take ~48 business hours.

Best,
Emma Tan
Marketplace Billing Operations
billing@marketplace.example.com

---
Attachments: usage_report_202609.csv (CSV stub), invoice_202609_marketplace.pdf (PDF stub)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Apportionment/proration for Sept — GCP + Azure listing overlap

Karthik / Laura / Rishi — forwarding billing's response and CSV. Key points: marketplace does not dedupe across listings by default and used UTC timestamps which likely caused the 17th–19th overlap.

Ask: can we either 1) accept their dedup job and have them issue a marketplace credit memo (preferred) OR 2) run an internal apportionment and absorb/reclass the payout difference between our GCP and Azure entity buckets? AtlasHealth wants a customer-facing note and either an immediate credit against Oct payout or a corrected invoice to avoid downstream payment disputes.

I attached the CSV they sent (see thread) and HubSpot deal 56432 for context.

Thanks — can each of you reply with feasibility and preferred path by EOD tomorrow?

—Irene

Subject: Re: Fwd: Apportionment/proration for Sept — GCP + Azure listing overlap

Team — quick notes from finance perspective after a skim of the CSV:

- Preliminary finding: ~12.4% of September's billed marketplace revenue for AtlasHealth is attributable to the overlapping timestamps (rough calc based on per-sku/day usage). If we accept the marketplace dedupe job, that should translate to a credit equal to that percent of the Sept invoice.
- VAT/tax: AtlasHealth is EU legal entity? (HubSpot shows region "US-EAST" but invoicing entity is ATLH GmbH). If the seller entity is EU-registered, we need the marketplace to include VAT breakdown on the corrected invoice; otherwise we will need to produce a VAT reallocation memo for our AP team.
- Accounting treatment: prefer to have the marketplace issue the external credit memo (so we don't have to book a contra-revenue adjustment internally). If they cannot, we can book a receivable from the seller and apply an internal intercompany adjustment across our ledger.

I'll draft a short tax memo (attached) for jurisdiction guidance and a proposed journal if we need to apply an internal correction.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Manager, Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>

Date: 2026-10-21T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Apportionment/proration for Sept — GCP + Azure listing overlap

Thanks all — proposed path:

1) We authorize Marketplace Billing to run the dedupe job and return a corrected CSV + credit memo draft. Ask them to include VAT line-items and to mark the credit \"Customer credit — proration overlap 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-19\".
2) If the credit memo includes VAT, have billing route the corrected invoice + credit to AtlasHealth directly and copy our AP inbox so the credit flows into our payout reconciliation (preferred).
3) Contingency: if marketplace cannot include VAT breakdown, we accept their credit (as non-VAT) and Rishi/Finance will file the tax_reallocation_memo and book an intercompany adjustment to reclassify the payout between our cloud-entity buckets.

Irene — please confirm you want me to ask them to proceed with the dedupe job (48 business hours) and to include a DocuSign amendment link for the AtlasHealth contract (small amendment to listing mapping). If yes I'll draft the customer note and send the external ask.

Karthik Iyer
Marketplace Partnerships — Redwood Inference
